_about: Mass growth allowance tables and the hidden growth distribution. Percent of basic mass.

mga_percent.source: ANSI/AIAA R-020A-1999, Recommended Practice for Mass Properties Control for Satellites, Missiles, and Launch Vehicles, Table 1, as printed in NASA/TM-2010-216218 (McGuire and Oleson, COMPASS Final Report: Low Cost Robotic Lunar Lander, NTRS 20110004181), Table 2.2, PDF p. 11. AIAA S-120-2006 and S-120A-2015 keep this table's structure (maturity codes E1/E2/C3/C4/A5/A6); S-120A itself is paywalled. Rows: E estimated (preliminary sketches), L layout (or major modification of existing hardware), P pre-release drawings (or minor modification), C released drawings, X existing hardware (actual mass from another program), A actual mass (measured flight hardware).

system_margin.source: AIAA S-120A-2015 Table 2 (mass risk assessment), as tailored in SMC-T-002 (16 Jul 2018), Sec. 5.1.10: at the proposal milestone, MGA above 15% plus mass margin above 15% (MGA + margin above 30%) is graded green. NASA COMPASS carries growth up to 30% of dry mass (NTRS 20110004181, Sec. 2.3).

growth_distribution.source: Hidden growth g of one category of one part, as a fraction of basic mass: lognormal with its median at the layout-row MGA and its 90th percentile at the estimated-row MGA, so sigma_ln = ln(E/L) / 1.2816 (0.316 for structure, thermal, propulsion and mechanisms). A team design is a parametric concept (S-120A maturity 'estimated'), so the allowance an S-120A mass engineer would carry, the E row, covers 9 parts in 10. Existing hardware (catalog engines, RTGs): median at the X row, same sigma_ln. Why not larger: the historical growth of whole programs is larger (mean 28% over 36 vehicles, 30% of them above 32.5%: Wilhite, Acta Astronautica 66, 2010, doi:10.1016/j.actaastro.2009.10.013, abstract; Mercury 30%, Gemini 18%, Apollo CM about 50%: Heineman, NASA TN D-6349, 1971, PDF p. 37; NRO unit-level growth 1.5 to 2 times the S-120 'estimated' MGA: MacKenzie and Burgess, ICEAA 2016, slide 13), but those include changed requirements, which the slides say MGA does not cover, and this game's requirements never change.

category_of_item._note: Each vehicle.py mass_breakdown item maps to one R-020A column, or to null when it is not hardware that grows (propellant, pressurant gas, ballast picked by the team).

weighing.source: A weighing reveals the as-built dry mass of one element. 0.1% (1 sigma) is an assumption for load-cell platform scales; the MSFC mass uncertainty slides give the remaining measured-mass uncertainty (A6) as about 0.1% to 0.2% (NTRS 20130014267, slide 4). Cost: a flight-like article must be built first, so a quarter of the element's cost plus a fixed fee (a game number, like the other test costs).
